thesis: The Release Gate must be a small, executable contract — a pure reference implementation plus a fixture suite that IS the specification — because prose specs of adversarial mechanisms structurally cannot converge. The current section in docs/specs/epic-1/spec.md § 'Release Gate for v1.0.0' is ~280 lines that took 26 adversarial review rounds precisely because every finding (#887, #909, #922, #923, #925, #934, #938, #939, #941, #942, #952, #953, #964, #969, #995, #996, #997, #1014, #1015, #1031, #1080, #1081, #1082) had to be patched into English, and English has no type checker: each patch created new ambiguous surface for the next round to attack ('anchored regex, not a glob' #1014 is a bug class that literally cannot exist in code with a test). Note what actually happened across those 26 rounds: every single surviving rule was forced to become machine-decidable anyway — the spec already says 'every criterion below is machine-decidable as written'. The review process was groping toward an executable contract while being forced to express it in the one medium that can't be executed. So execute it: extract the entire pass/fail predicate into one pure module, encode every reviewed adversarial scenario as a fixture (evidence in, verdict out), shrink the markdown to ~20 lines of intent plus a pointer, and change the amendment protocol so a reviewer finding against the gate lands as a FAILING FIXTURE plus the code change that greens it — never as a prose amendment. Fixtures end review ping-pong because a fixture is falsifiable: round N+1 cannot re-litigate round N's rule by reinterpreting a sentence, it must produce an evidence file on which the reference implementation returns the wrong verdict. Disagreement becomes `node gate-core.mjs evidence.json`, which terminates; disagreement about prose does not. Every anti-laundering rule that cannot be expressed as a deterministic function over recorded evidence gets CUT, not documented — an unexecutable rule in a gate spec is a false promise of enforcement.
design: MODULE — `hooks/lib/release-gate/` with a hard collect/decide seam: (1) `evidence-collect.sh` — the ONLY component that touches the network; runs the fully-paginated GraphQL queries (LabeledEvent/UnlabeledEvent timelines, closedByPullRequestsReferences, MarkedAsDuplicateEvent chains, commit signature verification objects, MAINTAINERS.md at the release-branch tip SHA) plus git queries (squash-commit messages on default branch, diff hunks in old-file coordinates) and emits one canonical `evidence.json` (sorted keys, LF, UTF-8, `schemaVersion` field). (2) `gate-core.mjs` — a PURE function `decide(evidence) -> verdict`: no I/O, no clock (the 2026-07-29 baseline is a constant carried in evidence), no env reads. (3) `gate-report.mjs` — verdict -> canonical `gate-report.json` + SHA-256 of exact bytes. (4) `hooks/scripts/release-gate.sh` — the CI entrypoint the release-captain runs, gluing collect -> decide -> report; sits under `hooks/scripts/**` so the existing ≥95% coverage floor already applies to it.

VERDICT VOCABULARY — `PASS` | `FAIL` (with the named criteria that failed and per-criterion evidence refs) | `BLOCKED` (with the open prerequisite issue numbers #419/#420/#510/#511/#649). The current spec's 'this criterion is not evaluable until #649/#511 closes' narrative becomes a mechanical BLOCKED verdict instead of prose caveats.

FIXTURES ARE THE SPEC — `tests/fixtures/release-gate/<NNNN-slug>/{evidence.json,expected.json,why.md}`, one directory per adversarial scenario, named by the review finding that motivated it: `0887-strip-label-exits-set/`, `0909-downrank-then-close/`, `0922-p1-applied-before-baseline-interval/`, `0923-far-hunk-cannot-vouch/`, `0939-duplicate-onto-unfloored-target/`, `0941-branch-only-commit-message/`, `0942-old-file-coordinates/`, `0995-no-witness-self-certification/`, `0997-prose-location-prefix-half-match/`, `1014-bot-regex-glob-inversion/`, `1031-insertion-only-guard-fix/`, `1080-signer-not-author-field/`, `1081-security-below-confirmed-high-floor/`, `1082-same-pr-later-round-with-witness/`, plus the happy paths (clean pass, legitimate down-rank reported, duplicate chain terminating open, no-PR-link remediation commit). `why.md` is one paragraph max: provenance and the attack the fixture forbids. The 26-round PR-description ledger maps 1:1 onto fixture directories — the review history becomes a regression suite instead of an archaeology exercise.

RUNNER — `tests/release-gate.contract.test.sh`, wired into `tests/run-suite.sh` (matching the repo's existing `*.contract.test.sh` convention): iterate fixtures, run `node hooks/lib/release-gate/gate-core.mjs --evidence <dir>/evidence.json`, deep-diff the verdict against `expected.json`. Because gate-core is pure, the suite is hermetic, offline, and fast — it runs on every commit under the TDD law, so the gate's own semantics are regression-locked at every green receipt.

REPLAYABILITY — every real gate run uploads BOTH `evidence.json` and `gate-report.json` as CI artifacts. Any disputed verdict is settled by replaying the recorded evidence through the pinned gate-core version and getting byte-identical output (and therefore the identical SHA-256 the acknowledgment binds to). The hash-acknowledgment mechanism the spec already defines (gateReportHash in `.factory/state/release-intent.json`; `factory-ops/release/<version>/confirmed-high.ack` with verified-signature human witness) keeps working unchanged — it just acknowledges the output of a reproducible function instead of a hand-audited report.

AMENDMENT PROTOCOL (the load-bearing process change) — a reviewer finding against the gate is admissible ONLY as a failing fixture: PR commit 1 adds `tests/fixtures/release-gate/<NNNN-new-attack>/` and the suite goes red; commit 2 changes gate-core and the suite goes green. This is exactly the repo's existing TDD law applied to the gate itself. A finding that cannot be expressed as an evidence file with a wrong verdict is by definition not a defect in a machine-decidable gate — it is either a producer-side convention (route it to the relevant charter/agent doc) or an opinion (close it). Prose amendments to gate semantics are rejected in review as a category. Gate-SCOPE changes (what blocks v1.0.0 at all) still require a numbered ADR per ADR 0005's owner rules — but the ADR points at fixtures, it does not restate predicates.

SPEC TEXT — docs/specs/epic-1/spec.md § 'Release Gate for v1.0.0' shrinks to approximately these 20 lines: '## Release Gate for v1.0.0 — Intent: v1.0.0 ships only when zero bug issues are open; zero P0/P1 tech-debt is open; zero issue that has ever carried `security` or `gate:confirmed-high` is open; every tech-debt issue is triaged (fail-closed); no gate-relevant issue has been closed since 2026-07-29 without a mechanically verified fix or qualifying duplicate; prerequisites #419/#420/#510/#511/#649 are closed; coverage, nightly-eval, and freeze-marker artifact checks hold; and the gate report is hash-acknowledged (with a verified-signature human second principal for any floored exemption). The NORMATIVE definition of every predicate above is executable, not prose: `hooks/lib/release-gate/gate-core.mjs` (pure: evidence in, verdict out) is the specification; `hooks/lib/release-gate/evidence-collect.sh` records the evidence (fully paginated; the snapshot is a CI artifact, so every verdict replays offline); `tests/fixtures/release-gate/` holds one fixture per adversarial scenario and `tests/release-gate.contract.test.sh` runs them in the suite. Amendments: a finding against the gate lands as a failing fixture plus the gate-core change that greens it — never as prose; if any document disagrees with the code and fixtures, the code and fixtures govern. Scope changes require an ADR (ADR 0005 owner rules), which points at fixtures. Verdicts: PASS, FAIL(criteria), BLOCKED(open prerequisites).' ROADMAP M4 and PRODUCT.md keep their one-line pointers; there is no second predicate copy anywhere, so tri-document drift (the original #444 review finding) becomes structurally impossible rather than procedurally forbidden.

EVIDENCE SCHEMA IS VERSIONED — `schemaVersion` in evidence.json; gate-core refuses (BLOCKED verdict) on a schema it does not know. Collector and core can therefore evolve independently, and old CI artifacts remain replayable against the gate-core version that judged them (pinned by the repo SHA of the run).
kept_mechanisms: Ever-carried set membership from LabeledEvent timelines for `bug`/`tech-debt`/`security`/`gate:confirmed-high`; current-state reads for P0–P3 only (#887) — as `everCarried(timeline, label)` over recorded events.

All open-issue criteria: zero open bug; zero open P0/P1 tech-debt; zero open ever-carried security (cross-priority, per ADR 0005); zero open ever-carried gate:confirmed-high; fail-closed triage with exact-case labels, most-severe-wins, legacy-label rejection.

Close-laundering audit over closes since 2026-07-29: gate-relevance via ever-carried sets plus interval-computed P0/P1 presence in [baseline, close] from Labeled/Unlabeled event intervals, not event dates (#922, #909).

Exemption (a): stateReason=completed + merged qualifying change (closedByPullRequestsReferences OR the no-PR-link remediation commit on the default branch, #894), non-empty whitespace-ignoring diff, source-pr trailer inequality with the #1082 same-PR branch (strict location + human witness), fail-closed on missing/unparseable source-pr trailer.
Fingerprint binding (i): citation in immutable evidence only — the squash commit's message as it exists on the default branch (#941); PR bodies rejected as post-merge-editable.

Location binding (ii): fully-anchored `^[A-Za-z0-9._/-]+:[0-9]+$` grammar (#997), hunk overlap in OLD-file coordinates within ±20 (#942), delete/replace OR insertion-point branch (#1031), fail-closed (not citation-only fallback) for grammar-nonconforming locations pending #649 (#995), renamed/deleted-path naming rule — this whole cluster is the poster child for code-over-prose: it is a pure function over recorded diff hunks and took roughly six review rounds to pin down in English.

Exemption (b): duplicate via most-recent MarkedAsDuplicateEvent, transitive chain to a terminal gate-relevant issue, cycle/non-termination fail-closed, floor-label inheritance on the terminal target (#939).
Down-rank visibility: every post-baseline P0/P1 -> P2/P3 down-rank listed by name in gate-report.json (#909).

Hash-acknowledgment machinery: canonical gate-report.json, SHA-256 of exact bytes, gateReportHash in `.factory/state/release-intent.json` (#934, #938, #952), and the two-principal rule for floored exemptions — verified-signature identity (signature.signer.login, state VALID, author=committer=signer, MAINTAINERS.md 'Human maintainers' roster pinned at the gate-run SHA, anchored bot-regex rejection) as a function over the recorded commit-verification object (#996, #1014, #1015, #1080, #1081).

Prerequisite state check: #419/#420/#510/#511/#649 closed, with their closes subject to the same close audit (satisfiable by construction per #925) — expressed as a BLOCKED verdict, not prose caveats.

Artifact checks: ≥95% coverage on hooks/scripts/** and hooks/lib/common.sh at the release-branch tip SHA; three consecutive green nightly-eval runs (BLOCKED until #511 lands thresholds); the single-line `**Freeze state: ON**` marker predicate over docs/PRODUCT.md content.

Heuristic floor for fingerprint-less hand-filed issues (merged non-empty-diff closing PR) — kept as a function; its 'this is a floor, not a proof' honesty moves from spec prose into the fixture's why.md and the risks table.
cut_mechanisms: The ~280 lines of normative prose themselves — every rule that survives does so as code + fixtures; prose restatements of adversarial predicates are the defect, not the documentation.
The inline finding-number narrative ledger woven through the spec (#887...#1082 with rationale asides) — provenance moves to one `why.md` per fixture; a spec section is not a review changelog.

Unverifiable review-quality obligations ('/ship records the field AFTER the release-captain REVIEWS the report'; the human 'reviewing' the down-rank report) — the gate can verify the recorded acknowledgment, never the quality of the reading; the ack functions stay, the review-happened claims go.

Cross-document producer obligations embedded in gate text ('the fix-side obligation lives in agents/implementer.md step 6', 'the clerk charter now mandates', 'its required-field list mandates it') — producer conventions live in the producer's charter file; the gate judges only recorded evidence and must not normatively define other documents' contents.

Charter-authorization commentary ('stripping tech-debt is not a ranking act any charter authorizes') — moot: everCarried() makes stripping mechanically ineffective, so the appeal to authority is dead weight.

Editorial honesty asides as normative text ('Residual risk, stated: ...', 'stated honestly as a heuristic floor') — residual risks become a short non-normative risks table plus fixtures demonstrating the accepted gap (e.g. a near-line cosmetic-insertion fixture whose expected verdict is PASS-with-report, documenting the accepted hole executably).

Implementation-detail prose that only exists to forbid a coding mistake (the anchored-regex-not-glob paragraph for the bot identity, #1014; the 'anchored at both ends' location-grammar paragraph, #997) — these are unit tests, not specification sentences; fixture 1014 and fixture 0997 replace them at zero ambiguity.

Tri-document mirroring rules and their enforcement prose (ROADMAP mirrors by reference, PRODUCT points at spec, 'if any summary diverges the spec governs') — collapsed to bare pointers; with one executable definition there is nothing left to drift.
Any FUTURE rule that cannot be phrased as evidence-in/verdict-out — cut at review time by construction: the amendment protocol physically cannot admit it, which is the point.
migration: PR #444 lands under this stance in the same PR, as three commits obeying the repo's TDD law: (1) `test:` — add `tests/fixtures/release-gate/` with ~40 fixtures transposed mechanically from the 26-round review ledger (each confirmed finding -> one fixture; each happy path -> one fixture) plus `tests/release-gate.contract.test.sh` wired into run-suite.sh — suite goes red; (2) `feat:` — add `hooks/lib/release-gate/{gate-core.mjs,gate-report.mjs,evidence-collect.sh}` and `hooks/scripts/release-gate.sh` until the suite is green — this IS the M4 'Release Gate script' work item, pulled forward, because under contract-first the spec and the script are the same deliverable and writing them twice (once in English, once in bash) is the cost bug CLAUDE.md tells us to file; (3) `docs:` — shrink spec.md § 'Release Gate for v1.0.0' to the ~20-line pointer text above, keep ADR 0005 untouched (it decides scope, not predicates — exactly the division this stance wants), add one ADR row widening the ≥95% coverage floor to `hooks/lib/release-gate/**` (same precedent as ADR 0005's common.sh widening; qa owns the threshold). The current 280-line section is not discarded — it is the requirements document the fixtures are transcribed FROM, and it retires with honor into the PR description. Review rounds 27+ change shape immediately: REQUEST CHANGES on the gate must attach a fixture directory demonstrating the wrong verdict, or it routes to a charter/product doc instead. The evidence collector is deliberately thin and separately tested against recorded GraphQL response fixtures (same recorded-data discipline), so #419/#420-class pagination bugs are contract-tested at the seam rather than re-litigated in prose.
risks_accepted: A bug in gate-core is normatively binding until a fixture catches it — the reference implementation being the spec means implementation bugs ARE spec bugs. Accepted: prose has the same failure mode with worse detection (26 rounds of it), and here detection is a red test, not a 27th review round.

The collect/decide seam is the trust boundary: a compromised or wrong evidence-collect.sh yields a 'correct' verdict over false facts, and the purity of gate-core proves nothing about collection fidelity. Mitigated by recorded-response contract tests on the collector and by evidence.json being an auditable CI artifact; residual risk accepted and it is where a hostile reviewer should aim.

JSON fixtures are less legible to a human maintainer than prose; the narrative shrinks to why.md one-liners. Accepted deliberately: the gate's audience is CI and adversarial reviewers, and legibility-to-attackers of exact semantics beats readability of approximate ones.

Cut producer-side obligations (implementer step 6, clerk trailer mandates) must find homes in their own charter files or they silently lapse, leaving future findings fingerprint-less and stuck at the heuristic floor. Accepted: that is the correct pressure — the gate should get stricter evidence by producers improving, not by the gate pretending prose obligations are enforcement.

Pulling the Release Gate script implementation into PR #444 makes it a bigger PR than a docs-only redesign. Accepted: the alternative is shipping a 27th prose draft and paying for rounds 28-40 on it, which is exactly the sprint-4 headline finding (the loop manufacturing debt faster than it resolves) this panel exists to stop.
One more coverage-floor widening ADR row is process overhead. Accepted: trivial next to the review-round cost it retires.
killerFeature: Review ping-pong ends structurally: a finding against the gate is admissible only as a failing fixture, so every dispute terminates in `bash tests/run-suite.sh` going red or not — the 26-round prose-patch loop becomes a regression suite that runs on every commit, and the 26 rounds already paid for become 40 permanent tests instead of 280 lines nobody can safely edit.
biggestRisk: The evidence collector: gate-core's purity guarantees nothing if evidence.json is collected wrong (pagination, timeline completeness, signature-object fidelity), and a hostile reviewer will correctly say the god-spec didn't disappear — part of it moved into a bash script at the network boundary where fixtures are only as good as the recorded responses they were transcribed from.
